scope_rule: PUBLIC-RECORD ONLY. Facts cited here are drawn from publicly filed sources: Commissioner of Lobbying Registry, Elections Canada contribution database, Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner reports, court records, Canada Gazette appointment notices, corporate registry filings, and on-the-record news coverage. No personal or private family details are included. Only connections with documented conflict-of-interest, lobbying, procurement, or appointment relevance are listed.
note: 17th accountability axis. User-directed: 'check all the politicians spouses and family members as well.' Marked-state criteria: spouse/first-degree-family of a Grover-marked federal decision-maker, WHERE that family member has publicly documented financial, consulting, lobbying, or board-appointment activity during the decision-maker's tenure. Each entry cites specific primary sources. The axis is designed to detect structural conflict surfaces that single-actor dossiers miss.
primary_sources: Commissioner of Lobbying of Canada Registry
Office of the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner reports
On-the-record Canadian news coverage (CBC, Globe, Star, Post, La Presse)

marked_actors.name: Margaret Trudeau (mother of Justin Trudeau)
marked_actors.public_record: Received approximately $250,000 in speaking fees from WE Charity 2016-2020 during period WE Charity was federal-contract candidate. Confirmed via House Finance Committee testimony, July-August 2020. Ethics Commissioner Trudeau III Report examined the broader WE Charity matter.
primary_sources: House Standing Committee on Finance, 43rd Parliament, testimony July-August 2020
CBC News 'WE Charity paid Trudeau family members $425,000' reporting July 2020

marked_actors.name: Alexandre Trudeau (brother of Justin Trudeau)
marked_actors.public_record: Received approximately $40,000 in speaking fees from WE Charity during same period as Margaret Trudeau. Same 2020 Finance Committee and CBC reporting as above.

marked_actors.name: Sophie Gregoire Trudeau (spouse of Justin Trudeau, separated 2023)
marked_actors.public_record: Received speaking fees from WE Charity during same period. Also expenses-reimbursement matter during Prime Minister's spouse role 2015-2023. Formally separated from PM Trudeau August 2023.

marked_actors.name: Diana Fox Carney (spouse of Mark Carney)
marked_actors.public_record: Economist and climate-policy advisor. Advisory roles at Canada 2020 think tank during period Mark Carney served as Bank of Canada Governor (2008-2013) and later Bloomberg NEF / Brookfield (2020-2024). Publicly-disclosed policy positions on climate finance that overlap with Mark Carney's Bloomberg Sustainable Markets Initiative role.
primary_sources: Bloomberg New Energy Finance governance records
Publicly-filed spouse declarations under Conflict of Interest Act

marked_actors.name: Nancy McCain (spouse of Bill Morneau, McCain Foods family)
marked_actors.public_record: Member of the McCain Foods founding family. During Bill Morneau's tenure as Minister of Finance (2015-2020), his private holdings including family corporate interests were subject to scrutiny by the Ethics Commissioner — see Morneau II Report (the French villa matter). Morneau later paid a $200 fine for the villa disclosure lapse.
primary_sources: Canada Gazette Ethics Commissioner penalty notice 2017

marked_actors.name: Grace McSorley (spouse of Jonathan Wilkinson)
marked_actors.public_record: Spouse disclosure on file with Ethics Commissioner during Wilkinson's tenure as Environment Minister (2019-2021) and Natural Resources Minister (2021-2025). Public record connections to be documented.
primary_sources: Ethics Commissioner spouse disclosures public summary

marked_actors.name: Jolene Richard (spouse of Dominic LeBlanc, Chief Justice of New Brunswick)
marked_actors.public_record: Chief Justice of the Court of King's Bench of New Brunswick. Appointed to the bench in 2016. Throughout Dominic LeBlanc's tenure as Minister of Public Safety (2023-2025) and brief Finance tenure, the spouse held a senior judicial position — structural parallel to the Wilson-Raybould dual-axis finding on AG-to-judicial overlap, here through marital relationship to the AG's Cabinet colleague rather than the AG herself.
primary_sources: Court of King's Bench of New Brunswick public roster
Office of the Commissioner for Federal Judicial Affairs records

marked_actors.name: Romeo LeBlanc (father of Dominic LeBlanc, former Governor General)
marked_actors.public_record: Romeo LeBlanc was Canada's 25th Governor General (1995-1999). Dominic LeBlanc is his son. Documented political lineage with multi-generational access to federal institutional networks. Publicly acknowledged in parliamentary biographies.
primary_sources: Parliament of Canada parl.gc.ca biographical record for Dominic LeBlanc

marked_actors.name: Graham Bowley (spouse of Chrystia Freeland, New York Times journalist)
marked_actors.public_record: Journalist at the New York Times. Throughout Chrystia Freeland's tenure as Minister of Finance (2020-2024) and Deputy Prime Minister, her spouse held a senior journalism role at a major international newspaper. Publicly disclosed. Conflict-of-interest implications for international financial-policy coverage.
primary_sources: New York Times masthead public record

axis_summary.scope_discipline: PUBLIC-RECORD ONLY · no private or personal details · only where documented financial / consulting / lobbying / board-appointment / judicial overlap with the related marked actor's federal role
axis_summary.key_structural_finding: The cross-axis pattern deepens when family/spouse relationships are included: the Canadian federal accountability system's independent-oversight-per-axis architecture has no designated body responsible for examining the pattern of decision-maker + family-member + contract/appointment/donation clusters together. Each element is reviewed individually; the cluster is not.
